record.paper_title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary
record.context_brief: topological type from convex planar boundary
record.original_question: Let C be a simple closed convex curve contained in a plane P, and let Σ be a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in ℝ³ with boundary ∂Σ = C. If Σ lies entirely on one side of P, must Σ be a topological disk?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Let C be a simple closed convex curve in a plane P. Let Σ be a compact embedded cmc surface in ℝ³ with ∂Σ=C. Assuming that Σ lies in one side of P, is Σ a topological disk?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a plane and let $C \subset P$ be a simple closed convex curve. A compact surface $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is said to have constant mean curvature (CMC) if its mean curvature function is constant, and it is embedded if the inclusion $\Sigma \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ is injective. Suppose $\Sigma$ is a compact embedded CMC surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary $\partial \Sigma$ equals $C$, and assume $\Sigma$ lies entirely in one of the two closed half-spaces determined by $P$. Must $\Sigma$ be a topological disk?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in recent surveys on compact CMC surfaces with boundary. Partial results exist: under additional hypotheses such as local convexity, the surface must be a spherical cap (hence a disk), and analogous results have been proved for special Weingarten surfaces with planar convex boundary. The general case for embedded CMC surfaces remains open.

status_evidence.title: Special Weingarten surfaces with planar convex boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Compact, connected, embedded Special Weingarten surfaces in ℝ³ with planar convex boundary are shown to be topological disks under suitable assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Related topological-disk conclusions are obtained only under additional Weingarten/convexity hypotheses, indicating the pure CMC case is not settled.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: A locally convex, embedded, compact, connected CMC hypersurface bounded by a closed strictly convex planar curve must be a spherical cap.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer is known under the extra assumption of local convexity, but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (Lopez)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys conjectures and partial results on whether embedded CMC surfaces bounded by a planar convex curve and lying on one side must be spherical caps/disks.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is discussed as an open conjecture in the CMC-with-boundary literature.
